panels.title: Total Cost
panels.description: FIXED: was a bare sum() of the raw counter, which shows the CURRENT process's cumulative value regardless of the time picker - and actually UNDERCOUNTS, since the counter resets on every new Claude Code process and a bare sum only sees whichever process last reported. increase(...[$__range]) correctly totals cost accrued within the selected window, counter-reset-safe (proven: bare sum stayed flat at $7.84 across 1h/24h/7d pickers; increase() correctly returned $40.59/$122/$677 for the same three).

panels.title: Total Tokens
panels.description: FIXED: was a bare sum() of the raw counter - ignored the time picker and undercounted across process restarts. Now increase(...[$__range]), matching Total Cost's fix.

panels.title: Cache Hit %
panels.description: Share of tokens served from prompt cache vs fresh. High = long sessions replaying big context repeatedly - this is the single biggest lever on spend.

panels.title: Sessions in Range
panels.description: FIXED: distinct session_ids with token activity in range. The old query summed claude_code_session_count_total, a counter that stays near-flat regardless of how many sessions actually ran (it read 1 while 8 sessions were active) - not a true concurrency or range count.

panels.title: Active Time
panels.description: FIXED: was a bare sum() of the raw counter - ignored the time picker and undercounted across process restarts. Now increase(...[$__range]).

panels.title: Priciest Session
panels.description: CHANGED from raw token count to dollar cost: "51.0 Mil" tokens is an abstract number with no reference point for whether that's fine or a problem; a dollar figure is something you can judge at a glance. The single most expensive session right now - see the Top Sessions table below for which one and its full breakdown.

panels.title: Tokens by Type Over Time
panels.description: input/output/cacheRead/cacheCreation. cacheRead dominating = long-running session replaying context every turn.

panels.title: Tokens by Model x Type Over Time
panels.description: Same breakdown split per model - spot a model switch shifting the token mix.

panels.title: Token Volume Over Time by Model
panels.description: Spot a model switch: usage shifting from one model to another over time.

panels.title: Model Comparison

targets.expr: avg by (model) (avg_over_time({service_name=~".+"} | event_name="api_request" | session_id=~"$session.*" | unwrap duration_ms [$__range]))

(sum by (model) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+"} | event_name="api_error" | session_id=~"$session.*" [$__range])) or (sum by (model) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+"} | event_name=~"api_request|api_error" | session_id=~"$session.*" [$__range])) * 0)) / sum by (model) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+"} | event_name=~"api_request|api_error" | session_id=~"$session.*" [$__range]))
quantile_over_time(0.5, {service_name=~".+"} | event_name="api_request" | session_id=~"$session.*" | unwrap duration_ms [$__range]) by (model)
quantile_over_time(0.95, {service_name=~".+"} | event_name="api_request" | session_id=~"$session.*" | unwrap duration_ms [$__range]) by (model)

panels.description: One row per model - everything you'd otherwise need five separate gauges to compare. Cache hit % and Error % are genuinely status metrics (good/bad), so they alone get the green/red treatment; the rest is plain magnitude. FIXED: Error % used to silently disappear from this table whenever a model had zero api_error events, because dividing by an empty vector in PromQL/LogQL yields no series at all - the numerator now falls back to an explicit 0 per model so the division always has something to divide. Added p50/p95 latency alongside the average, since a mean alone hides tail latency.

panels.title: MCP Tool Token Usage
panels.description: Per-MCP-tool token attribution (e.g. Grafana get_dashboard_by_uid vs narrower tools).

panels.title: Tool Usage Summary (calls, latency, output size, error rate)

targets.expr: avg by (tool_name) (avg_over_time({service_name=~".+"} | event_name="tool_result" | session_id=~"$session.*" | unwrap duration_ms [$__range]))
sum by (tool_name) (sum_over_time({service_name=~".+"} | event_name="tool_result" | session_id=~"$session.*" | unwrap tool_result_size_bytes [$__range]))

(sum by (tool_name) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+"} | event_name="tool_result" | session_id=~"$session.*" | success="false" [$__range])) or (sum by (tool_name) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+"} | event_name="tool_result" | session_id=~"$session.*" [$__range])) * 0)) / sum by (tool_name) (count_over_time({service_name=~".+"} | event_name="tool_result" | session_id=~"$session.*" [$__range]))

panels.description: MERGED from four separate panels (Tool Result Size, Tool Call Count, Avg Tool Duration bargauges + Tool Error Rate table) into one per-tool summary. One row per tool: call count (blue magnitude bar), average duration, total output bytes injected into context, and failure rate (green/red status). Error % uses the or-fallback-to-zero pattern so a tool with zero failures shows 0% instead of vanishing.

panels.title: Slowest Tool Calls (highest duration)
panels.description: Every claude_code.tool span (any tool), one row per call, slowest-first with a duration bar. full_command wraps to full multi-line and has a cell-inspect magnifier (click the icon to read the whole command in a modal). full_command is Bash-only and needs OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1; other tools still show duration + name. Filter by Tool via the column header.

panels.title: Bash Tool Calls (duration, result size, and command on one line)

targets.expr: {service_name=~".+"} | event_name="tool_result" | tool_name="Bash" | session_id=~"$session.*" | line_format "{{.tool_input}}" | json command="command" | line_format "{{.duration_ms}}ms {{if eq .success \"true\"}}OK{{else}}FAIL{{end}} ({{.tool_result_size_bytes}}B)  {{.command}}"

panels.description: FIXED: was a raw logs panel where every row just said "claude_code.tool_result", with the command/duration/result size hidden behind a click-to-expand. line_format now parses the bare command out of tool_input and bakes duration, OK/FAIL, and result size directly into the visible line. For a slowest-first ranking (not just chronological), see "Slowest Tool Calls" below, which sources the same data from traces.

panels.title: Time to First Token by Model
panels.description: TraceQL metrics run directly against Tempo span data. Tempo caps metrics queries at ~2-3h of range (confirmed: 120min works, 180min returns HTTP 400), so this panel is pinned to the last hour regardless of the dashboard time picker.

panels.title: Slowest User Prompts (highest turn duration)

targets.query: { name = "claude_code.interaction" && span.user_prompt != nil && span.user_prompt !~ "<.*" && span.session.id =~ "$session.*" } | select(span.user_prompt)

panels.description: The actual user prompt text for the slowest turns, one row per turn, slowest-first with a duration bar. Prompt text wraps in full and has a cell-inspect magnifier. Harness-injected turns (<task-notification>, slash-command scaffolding, etc.) are filtered out at query time (span.user_prompt !~ "<.*") so only real prompts rank. Requires OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1.

panels.title: Time Blocked on User Approval (permission wait, slowest first)
panels.description: FIXED: was Tempo-only with the decision nested. Now tableType=spans flattens duration + decision into columns. claude_code.tool.blocked_on_user wraps the wait for a permission prompt - pure human latency, not model or tool time. Large values here mean approval friction (you weren't at the keyboard), not agent slowness - a recommended agentic-UX KPI alongside model/tool latency.

panels.title: Subagent Delegation - LLM Calls Inside an Agent Tool Call

targets.query: { name = "claude_code.tool" && span.tool_name = "Agent" } >> { name = "claude_code.llm_request" } | select(span.model, span.input_tokens, span.output_tokens, span.duration_ms)

panels.description: Each subagent llm_request span (nested under a parent claude_code.tool where tool_name="Agent"), flattened via tableType=spans into real columns: model, input/output tokens, and a duration bar. Slowest-first. A busy Agent row here = heavy delegation.

panels.title: Trace Explorer (filtered by $session above) - click a Trace ID to open the full waterfall
panels.description: One row per trace for the selected $session, newest-first, with a duration bar. Click a Trace ID to open the full waterfall (interaction -> llm_request/tool -> tool.execution) in Explore. FIXED: the raw 'nested' spans blob column is now hidden; it was rendering as unreadable JSON.

panels.title: Top Sessions by Token Usage - with Cost & Active Time (pick a session_id prefix for the filter above)
panels.description: Deliberately NOT filtered by $session - this is the picker. One-hue magnitude ramp on the Tokens column (this is ranking, not status) - a handful of huge sessions dominating means restart/compact discipline is the fix. Cost and Active Time are joined in so you can tell a token-heavy-but-fast session (efficient) from a token-heavy-and-slow one (the actual long-session anti-pattern this row is named for).

panels.title: Sessions by Terminal Type
panels.description: Distinct sessions per terminal (ghostty vs tmux vs ...), as a donut so it stays readable regardless of how many terminal types appear. Built on token_usage (continuously re-exported) rather than the session-start counter, which goes stale within minutes.

panels.title: Compaction Events (auto-compact firing = context outgrew the window)

targets.expr: {service_name=~".+"} | event_name="compaction" | session_id=~"$session.*" | line_format "{{.trigger}}  pre={{.pre_tokens}}tok -> post={{.post_tokens}}tok  ({{.duration_ms}}ms)  session={{.session_id}}"

panels.description: FIXED: was an unreadable raw logs panel (every row just said "claude_code.compaction", detail hidden behind a click). line_format now bakes trigger/pre-post tokens/duration directly into the line - no expansion needed. Frequent auto-compactions on one session_id = it's running too long.

panels.title: Git Activity
panels.description: MERGED from the separate Commits Created + Pull Requests Created stats. round() wraps increase() because these are counts of discrete, sparse events - raw increase() extrapolates fractional values (e.g. 2.6 commits).

panels.title: API Errors & Exhausted Retries
panels.description: FIXED: was a raw logs panel needing a click per row; model/status/attempt/error are now baked into the visible line.
